customer_corp_ops: Hey @jordan_support — starting ~08:12 UTC our EU users (Frankfurt) hit 500s and a surge of 429s. Traces show requests landing in us-west instead of eu-central. P95 latency ~700ms. Can you check routing?

jordan_support: Thanks — can you paste a curl sample and a trace (dig + trace) from a Frankfurt client? Any client-side DNS caching? :thinking_face:

customer_corp_ops: Repro steps: on a Frankfurt box -> `dig +short api.redwood.com @1.1.1.1` returns `35.227.12.9` (us-west). Also tried `curl -v https://api.redwood.com/health -H "X-Test: eu-check"` and got `x-region: us-west` and 502s intermittently.

liam_sre: That's suspicious — looks like resolver is returning US anycast IP. Two quick checks: 1) `dig +short @<local-resolver> api.redwood.com` and 2) check EDNS Client Subnet (ECS) in the resolver path. Some ISPs strip ECS which can cause wrong POP selection.

priya_netops: I pulled our GeoIP DB version: `geoip/locations.json` timestamp 2026-02-28T03:50Z. CDN edge routing config shows `fallback_policy: region-prefer` (not strict). If the resolver returns an IP that looks global, fallback to lowest-cost pop might pick us-west.

jordan_support: @customer_corp_ops — can you run `dig +short @<your-resolver> api.redwood.com +edns=2` and `dig @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.com +bufsize=1232 +short`? Also include full output of `dig +trace` if possible.

customer_corp_ops: Paste of dig +trace (anonymized):
```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> +trace api.redwood.com
.           51492 IN NS a.root-servers.net.
... (skipping) ...
api.redwood.com.  30 IN A 35.227.12.9
```
Resolver seems to return 35.227.12.9 consistently. TTL from authoritative is 60s.

liam_sre: Two hypotheses: 1) Upstream resolver cache or ISP removed ECS info so authoritative geo-routing cannot pick eu pop -> returns a global IP that routes to us-west. 2) GeoIP DB mismatch for that client IP range. Also note TTL=60 means caches can propagate quickly — but if ISP has long resolver caching (ignoring TTL), it sticks.

priya_netops: I checked our edge logs for the client IP block (last octet masked): requests arriving to us-west with `x-origin-pop: us-west-2a` and `x-route-reason: resolver-unmapped`. We also have an S3 sync job that updates GeoIP on the control plane; last sync showed a transient 503 at 03:48Z which retried but may have left partial state. Filing internal ticket INF-4829.

monitor-bot: alert: geoip-sync failed at 2026-03-04T03:48:12Z (HTTP 503) — retry succeeded at 2026-03-04T03:53:02Z.

jordan_support: Good find. For immediate mitigation: 1) Lower DNS TTL to 30s for api.redwood.com so clients bounce faster, 2) Temporarily set `fallback_policy: region-strict` for eu-central to avoid cross-region fallbacks for EU requests, 3) Purge resolver prefill cache for that prefix in our CDN.

priya_netops: I'll push TTL change and override routing policy for the EU shard. Plan: set TTL=30 and apply `region-strict` to eu-central for 15 minutes, monitor. If we see <1% misroutes, rollback to normal. Also kicking off a forced geoip DB reapply from a cold copy.

liam_sre: Also add a short term WAF rule to respond with 429 -> 503 mapping? better to throttle back to avoid billing spike. But be careful with client-side retries.

customer_corp_ops: Appreciate it. Any ETA? We have paying customers affected.

jordan_support: ETA: TTL + routing change in ~6 mins. GeoIP reapply in ~20. I'll post updates.

monitor-bot: deploy-bot: routing-overrides/eu-strict enabled by user priya_netops at 2026-03-04T08:20:40Z — canary rollout 10% -> 100%

priya_netops: TTL lowered to 30s, `region-strict` applied to eu-central shard. Forcing geoip reapply now. Please retest from your Frankfurt box (clear local DNS cache first).

customer_corp_ops: Retest: `dig +short api.redwood.com @1.1.1.1` now returns `18.194.200.12` (eu pop). Curl shows `x-region: eu-central` and latency back to ~40ms. 429s gone. :tada:

jordan_support: Great. Follow-ups: 1) Investigate why the GeoIP sync returned transient 503 — add extra validation step to ensure atomic swap on control plane, 2) Add resolver-affinity telemetry to detect EDNS stripping earlier, 3) Consider making `region-prefer` opt-in per-customer rather than default. I created ENG-9031 for the validation and ENG-9032 for resolver-affinity telemetry.

priya_netops: Noted. We'll also add an alert if >0.5% of eu-originating requests are routed outside EU for >2m.

customer_corp_ops: Thanks everyone. Happy to help with extra traces if needed.

jordan_support: Closing this thread once ENG ops confirm geoip reapply passed. If anything recurs, please reopen. :thumbsup:
